# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — teach the hidden-replay generalization gap + type fidelity + verify-before-done
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md (cluster 1, KNOWLEDGE): new block "YOUR CODE IS RE-RUN ON HIDDEN DATA" — compute from the input at run time; never paste/cache preview values; never copy a "desired/answer/sample/after" sheet into the answer cells; derive row/col extents dynamically; base positions on headers.
  - prompt.md (cluster 2, OUTPUT-CONTRACT): new block "MATCH THE EXPECTED VALUE'S TYPE AND FORMAT" — numbers as numbers (no str()), copy exact casing of labels that exist elsewhere, preserve neighbor type, empty only when intended.
  - task_template.md (cluster 3, STRUCTURE): replaced the "once that file exists, you are done" line with a required verification round (re-open output, print answer_position, confirm present+typed+computed-not-hardcoded, else fix). "Done" now requires a passing read-back.
- Expected effect + safety:
  - Edit A targets the dominant `[1,0,0]`/`[1,1,0]` signature (passes instance 1, fails the text-substituted re-run on instances 2/3): 51262 (pasted 30/20/0), 50755 ([25,3,25,22,60]), 250-20 (copies "Desired outcome" sheet), 53957 (range(15,26)), 267-18, 58890, 32975, 48588, 49782, 30930. Safe because all 49 passing tasks scored [1,1,1] across 3 varying-data instances → they already generalize; the rule only describes existing good behavior.
  - Edit B targets 585-41 (str() coercion), 50486 ("Chep" vs sheet "CHEP"), 48983 (None vs empty). Additive; passing tasks already write correct types.
  - Edit C is structural, makes verification a precondition of finishing; passing tasks verify and stop with identical output. A formula cell reads back as a populated string, so the 5 passing formula tasks are untouched.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — seed-only; LEDGER/RUNMAP empty.
- Refuted hypotheses / NOT tried on purpose: did NOT add a global "never write Excel formulas / always write literal values" rule. 5 PASSING tasks (35747, 37962, 45581, 49237, 54675) pass BY writing formulas (LibreOffice recalcs them); and failing formula tasks ask for formulas just like the passing ones, so formula-vs-value is not a safe discriminator. Left the existing "prefer literal values" line as-is.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: bespoke algorithm/task-misinterpretation (~15 tasks: 39946, 53305, 32468, 6698, 47699, 14207, 4225, 34-5, 347-49, 146-49, 577-40, 413-15, 398-14, 55912, 55039). These are ambiguous-spec comprehension errors, not clean knowledge gaps. Candidate next lever: worked-example snippets for recurring sub-patterns — robust color/font detection (openpyxl rgb/indexed/theme), and reading existing formula results with data_only=True (47699 loaded data_only=False and never saw the values).
- ENVIRONMENT fault handed back: 45944 — feedback explicitly states "formula recalculation FAILED … Not a prompt defect — do not optimize against it." Did not work around it.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: if this is accepted, attack cluster 4 with worked examples (color detection, data_only reads) as BOUNDED additive method snippets, verifying each against its trace and confirming no passing color/formula task changes.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.560 Δ=+0.022 · fixed={44264, 48588, 50486, 50682, 51262, 53023, 53957, 55224} · broke={2768, 31420, 399-14, 42930, 56561, 58484}.
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.560 Δ=+0.022 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — breadth across cand_0001's deferred "bespoke" cluster + fix the 399-14 regression
- Changes I made (all additive; no global rule loosened):
  - prompt.md (cluster: input-extent, KNOWLEDGE): bullet in the RE-RUN block — answer_position bounds only WHERE you write, NOT the extent of the input; read/aggregate over ALL data rows, never bound the input loop by the answer range's last row or preview count. Targets 250-20, 30930, 32975.
  - prompt.md (cluster: composite-key/grouping, KNOWLEDGE): bullet — build keys from EVERY jointly-identifying column; detect groups by CONTIGUOUS runs and reset per boundary (no global value-keyed dict); never tie an output cell's position to a column/sheet the instruction says is unrelated. Targets 58890, 32975, 55912.
  - prompt.md (cluster: paraphrase, KNOWLEDGE): new block "REPRODUCE THE STATED OPERATION EXACTLY" — same operators/value set, POSITIONAL (not sorted/ranked) refs, Excel blank→0 in lookups/#N/A on miss, honor explicit cell refs, and detect color/bold in rich-text runs or CF rules (not cell.fill/font.color). Targets 6698, 50755, 48983, 14207.
  - prompt.md + task_template.md (cluster: empty-vs-zero, KNOWLEDGE+STRUCTURE): new block "BLANK vs ZERO" (write only where the op produces a value; "remain unchanged" ⇒ leave as-is, don't write 0/"-"; write 0 where an aggregate over blanks yields 0) AND refined verify item (a) so it no longer pressures filling genuinely-blank cells. Targets the 399-14 regression + 48983, 398-14.
  - prompt.md + task_template.md (cluster: examples, STRUCTURE): new block "USE ANY EXAMPLE AS A CHECK" + verify item (d) — reproduce the LOGIC that yields any stated/embedded example and confirm the output matches it, else revise (reproduce logic, never copy the sample). Targets 2768, 413-15, 32023, 39946.
- Expected effect + why safe: each rule DESCRIBES the behavior the 51 [1,1,1] passing tasks already exhibit (they generalize / match their examples / write correct blanks), so their trajectories don't change; additions are narrowing/knowledge, never a loosened decision. The one modified line (verify item (a)) is made MORE accurate, not more permissive, and reverses the exact over-fill that broke 399-14 under cand_0001 (agent wrote O=0 for "remain unchanged" rows).
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 ACCEPTED (fixed 8, broke 6). I am repairing one of its regressions (399-14, empty-vs-zero) and decomposing its deferred "cluster 4 (bespoke misreads)" into the six prose-fixable sub-patterns above. Did NOT touch the RE-RUN or TYPE/FORMAT blocks (they worked) beyond adding two bullets.
- Refuted hypotheses (never re-test): global "never use formulas / always literals" — cand_0001 note + 5 passing formula tasks (35747/37962/45581/49237/54675) prove formula-vs-value is not a safe discriminator. Left "prefer literals" untouched.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: volatile "current date" (32023, 34-5 — ambiguous snapshot vs today=2026-08-02); genuinely underspecified specs (55039, 53449, 53305, 10281, 254-34, 269-44). No safe general prose fix without leaking gold.
- Plateau signal: only one prior RESULT (accepted, +0.022) — not a plateau. Staying on the prompt lever (breadth of knowledge/structure additions) rather than switching to a code/tool lever.
- ENVIRONMENT faults handed back (do NOT optimize against): 45944 (known recalc), 53062 (48k-row recalc), 4225 & 55258 (output provably reproduces the instruction's own example yet [0,0,0] — grader/type fault).
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, watch which of the six clusters actually converted; if the empty-vs-zero refinement re-broke a task, redesign it as a pure knowledge rule without touching verify item (a). If rejected, bisect the five edits (the composite-key and example-check blocks are the least-certain) via the RESULT's broke set.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.571 Δ=+0.011 · fixed={2768, 31420, 347-49, 399-14, 47699, 50755, 56561} · broke={18137, 353-19, 36478, 45300, 50486, 53957}.
<!-- cand_0002: ACCEPTED val=0.571 Δ=+0.011 -->

## Iteration cand_0003 — boundary-segment edge-cases + unattended-re-run robustness (two additive prompt bullets; plateau documented)
- Changes I made (both prompt.md, both ADDITIVE, no global rule loosened, no deletion):
  - Edit B (cluster: run/segment generalization gap): extended the "runs of / delimited by /
    between-within markers" bullet to require handling the partial segment BEFORE the first
    marker and AFTER the last marker (a segment with no closing marker still needs its result
    emitted), back-to-back markers (empty segment), and a deterministic marker-row membership
    decision. Targets 30930, 32975, 58890, 58484, 42930, 250-20, 49782, 53305.
  - Edit A (cluster: unattended-re-run crash → no output): new bullet in the RE-RUN block —
    the same code re-runs on hidden inputs it never sees, so it must run to completion and
    reach the save on every one; an unexpected blank/text/date-as-string/shifted-header/
    row-count must not raise before output_path is written; save at the very end,
    unconditionally. Targets 353-19 (case 2 "produced NO output file").
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - Edit B: 30930 never emits the trailing segment (writes only on a closing marker); 32975
    resets a running max per run and mishandles a boundary — both pass preview [1] and fail
    the hidden variants. Naming the boundary cases to COVER (not a direction) fixes the drop
    without dictating include-vs-exclude. Safe: fires only on run/segment tasks; passing
    run/segment tasks are [1,1,1] and already handle their boundaries, so no flip.
  - Edit A: 353-19's hidden variant raised and saved nothing. Rule makes "run to completion +
    always save" explicit. Safe: passing tasks are [1,1,1] on all 3 instances → they never
    crash, so the robustness path never changes what they do; phrased as robustness, not
    "default the cell" (avoids silent wrong values).
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0002 ACCEPTED (fixed 7, broke 6). I kept every load-bearing
  block from cand_0001/cand_0002 and did NOT touch the "prefer literals" line or re-tighten
  verify item (a) (cand_0001's 399-14 over-fill regression). My edits are new, narrow, and
  in the RE-RUN block only.
- Refuted hypotheses (never re-test): global "never use formulas / always literals" (5 passing
  formula tasks disprove it); re-tightening verify item (a) to "every cell holds a value"
  (broke 399-14 under cand_0001).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: the large comprehension / ambiguous-spec [0,0,0]
  cluster (269-44, 34-5, 157-4, 577-40, 398-14, 413-15, 146-49, 267-18, 254-34, 36478, 45300,
  18137, 50526, 55912, 39946, 32468, 53449, 55039, 10281, 6698, 14207, 585-41, …). The agent's
  emitted code already generalizes — it implements the WRONG operation. No traces contain gold,
  so no interpretation can be VERIFIED; every prose fix here would fail the VERIFIED/SAFE tests
  and risk leaking a task-specific reading. Deliberately not touched.
- Plateau signal: Δ decayed +0.022 → +0.011; clean knowledge clusters are exhausted. If these
  two additive bullets don't clear the bar, the only untried lever is a single tight WORKED
  EXAMPLE (a canonical robust skeleton) — but it must NOT encode op-specific assumptions
  (never "clear the answer range first" → that reintroduces the 399-14 over-write). Beyond
  that the ceiling is comprehension, which prose cannot safely close without gold.
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, confirm which of the run/segment gen-gap tasks flipped and
  whether Edit A recovered 353-19; then attempt the worked-example skeleton lever. If rejected,
  the likelier culprit is Edit B (it touches run/segment reasoning that some passing task may
  share) — drop B, keep the pure-robustness Edit A, and re-check the broke set.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.637 Δ=+0.066 · fixed={18137, 267-18, 353-19, 36478, 45300, 50486, 53957} · broke={50755}.
<!-- cand_0003: ACCEPTED val=0.637 Δ=+0.066 -->

## Iteration cand_0004 — switch levers: make generalization an EXECUTED self-test, not more prose
- Changes I made (1 edit):
  - task_template.md, verification round (cluster: over-fit generalization / edge-case,
    STRUCTURE): new numbered step 4 "Generalization self-test". After writing output_path
    from the real input, the agent must load a scratch copy, MUTATE it to resemble a hidden
    variant (append rows past the last data row incl. a new group + a trailing partial group
    with no closing marker; change values; reorder/duplicate groups; insert a blank/
    text-where-number), re-run the SAME logic on the scratch copy to a throwaway path, and
    confirm it never raises, scans to the NEW last row, and gets the appended/trailing rows
    right — else derive extents/boundaries from the data, fix the GENERAL logic, and re-save
    output_path from the REAL input. Diagnostic-only; output_path is written FIRST.
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - Targets the RESPONSIVE `[1,0,0]`/`[1,0,1]` cluster (30930, 32975, 58890, 58484, 42930,
    250-20, 48983, 49782): these pass the preview (operation is right) but are over-fit and
    drop/misplace results on a hidden file with more rows or a leading/trailing partial
    group. The prompt already TELLS the agent to write general code and handle boundaries
    (cand_0002/0003 prose) — it skips it. This makes the agent EXERCISE the exact hidden-
    variant cases and observe the drop, so it fixes the over-fit before finishing.
  - Safe: output_path is written unconditionally from the real input BEFORE the self-test;
    the self-test writes only to a throwaway path. All 58 passing tasks are `[1,1,1]` on
    three varying-data instances → they already generalize, so on the scratch copy their
    code yields correct results, the self-test passes, and they finish with an identical
    saved file. ADDITIVE (a new step); nothing reworded/looser/deleted; no placeholder
    touched; no task-specific literal.
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0003 ACCEPTED (+0.066) proved the over-fit/boundary
  cluster is CONVERTIBLE (fixed 18137, 267-18, 353-19, 36478, 45300, 50486, 53957 via
  boundary + run-to-completion prose). This iteration escalates the SAME cluster from
  "told the rule" to "must run the test" — the untried WORKED-EXAMPLE/procedure lever
  cand_0003's PROCESS explicitly flagged as next. Kept every load-bearing block from
  cand_0001–0003 untouched.
- Refuted hypotheses (never re-test): global "never use formulas / always literals" (5
  passing formula tasks disprove it); re-tightening verify item (a) to "every cell holds a
  value" (broke 399-14 under cand_0001).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: comprehension / ambiguous-spec `[0,0,0]` (~16
  tasks: 269-44, 157-4, 577-40, 398-14, 413-15, 146-49, 32468, 39946, 53305, 53449, 55039,
  50526, 254-34, 6698, 10281, 34-5-partly). Code already generalizes; it implements the
  WRONG operation. No gold in the traces → no interpretation is VERIFIABLE; every prose fix
  here fails VERIFIED/SAFE and risks leaking a task-specific reading. Deliberately not
  touched. Also observed but skipped: 50755 SORTED despite the positional rule and 585-41
  wrote str despite the numbers-as-numbers rule — "rule present but skipped", i.e. NOT a
  knowledge gap; more prose would not help.
- Plateau signal: clean KNOWLEDGE clusters are exhausted; I switched from the prose/knowledge
  lever to the STRUCTURE/executed-check lever. If this self-test does not clear the bar, the
  residual is the comprehension ceiling, which cannot be safely closed without ground truth
  — next iteration should hand back that ceiling with the evidence rather than ship
  speculative comprehension prose.
- ENVIRONMENT faults handed back (do NOT optimize against): 14207 (recalc, feedback says so),
  45944, 53062, 55912 (unreadable xlsx), 4225, 55258.
- Focus next iteration: if ACCEPTED, confirm which over-fit tasks the self-test flipped and
  whether the self-test occasionally over-corrects a passing task (watch the broke set); if
  REJECTED, the likely cause is non-conversion (agent not running the test), not regression
  — consider promoting a one-line self-test cue into prompt.md, or conclude the comprehension
  ceiling and hand it back.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.560 Δ=-0.077 · fixed={—} · broke={18137, 253-22, 347-49, 47699, 50486, 53957, 56561}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
<!-- cand_0004: rejected val=0.560 Δ=-0.077 -->

## Iteration cand_0005 — one verified bounded fix for the type-canonicalized-key generalization sub-pattern
- Changes I made (1 edit):
  - prompt.md (new bullet after the composite-key bullet; cluster: match/group/lookup keys
    that mismatch across value TYPE on hidden data): "CANONICALIZE ANY KEY OR COMPARISON BY
    VALUE, NOT BY STORED TYPE" — don't key on `str(value)`, don't `==` mixed types
    (`str(1)`≠`str(1.0)`≠`"1"`, `1 == "1"` is False); coerce numeric parts to a number,
    strip+casefold text, reduce dates to their calendar day. Worked-caution style for the
    weaker reader.
- EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - Targets the `[1,0,*]` generalization gap tasks whose emitted code builds keys via
    `str(...)`/raw `==` (grep-confirmed): 48983 `[1,1,0]` (`key=«redacted»
    → int vs float miss), 58484 `[1,0,0]` (`original == operator_number` raw), 58890, 250-20,
    49782, 32975. These pass the preview (one stored type) and miss on a hidden file that
    stores the same value as float/text. The edit makes equal-in-Excel values compare equal
    in code, so the SAME code matches across all three graded inputs.
  - Safe/BOUNDED: canonicalization only makes values that ARE equal compare equal; it never
    splits a key or merges two genuinely-distinct values, so it cannot flip a match any
    passing task currently gets right. Passing lookup/group tasks are `[1,1,1]` on three
    varying-data instances → their keys already align; nothing changes for them. Additive
    bullet; no global rule reworded/looser/deleted; no task-specific literal.
- Building on prior RESULTS: kept every load-bearing block from cand_0001–0003 (RE-RUN /
  generalization, TYPE/FORMAT, verify-before-finish, BLANK-vs-ZERO, positional/exact,
  composite-key, boundary-segment, run-to-completion). Did NOT re-introduce cand_0004's
  executed "generalization self-test" (REJECTED, broke {18137, 253-22, 347-49, 47699, 50486,
  53957, 56561}).
- Refuted hypotheses (never re-test): global "never use formulas / always literals" (5
  passing formula tasks disprove it); re-tightening verify item (a) to "every cell holds a
  value" (broke 399-14 under cand_0001); an EXECUTED per-run self-test in task_template
  (cand_0004 REJECTED −0.077).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: comprehension / ambiguous-spec `[0,0,0]` (~15:
  269-44, 146-49, 157-4, 254-34, 398-14, 413-15, 577-40, 50526, 55039, 53449, 32468, 39946,
  6698, 50755, 585-41). Code generalizes but implements the WRONG operation; no gold in
  traces → unverifiable → every prose fix fails VERIFIED/SAFE. Boundary/trailing-segment
  prose already present (cand_0002/0003); restating is out of scope.
- Plateau signal: cand_0003 (+0.066) then cand_0004 REJECTED (structural escalation of the
  SAME generalization cluster backfired). Clean prose surface nearly exhausted; this
  iteration extracts the one remaining VERIFIABLE bounded generalization sub-pattern
  (type-canonicalized keys) via KNOWLEDGE+worked-example rather than another STRUCTURE push.
- ENVIRONMENT faults handed back (do NOT optimize against): 45944, 14207 (recalc), 53062
  (48k-row recalc), 4225, 55258 (grader/type fault, output reproduces the stated example),
  55912 (unreadable xlsx); volatile-date 34-5, 32023.
- Focus next iteration: if ACCEPTED, confirm which `[1,0,*]` key tasks flipped (expect
  48983/58484/58890/250-20). If REJECTED with no regressions, the residual is the
  comprehension ceiling — hand it back with the evidence rather than ship speculative
  comprehension prose. Do not re-attempt executed self-tests or global-rule rewrites.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.560 Δ=-0.077 · fixed={—} · broke={31420, 36478, 47699, 49237, 50486, 50682, 56561}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
<!-- cand_0005: rejected val=0.560 Δ=-0.077 -->

## Iteration cand_0006 — the one verifiable safe fix (macro/VBA graded on cell VALUES, not source); plateau/ceiling documented
- Changes I made (1 edit):
  - prompt.md (cluster: macro/VBA-phrased task, OUTPUT-CONTRACT/missing-rule): new bullet after
    the "prefer literal values" line — when the instruction says "write a macro/VBA/script,"
    the task is STILL graded only on the resulting cell VALUES in answer_position; do NOT write
    macro/VBA/script SOURCE TEXT (a `Sub … End Sub` block) into a cell; simulate in Python what
    the macro would do and write the resulting value(s). Targets 254-34.
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - 254-34 `[0,0,0]`: trace comment "Put a general VBA backtracking solution in C2" then
    `ws["C2"] = <Sub…End Sub string>`; gold C2 = numeric 994110. The rule reverses that exact
    decision (simulate + write the value). BOUNDED: grepped all 91 traces — 18 mention
    macro/VBA/script, 10 of them pass `[1,1,1]` and EVERY one already writes computed VALUES;
    254-34 is the ONLY trace embedding VBA source. Writing source text into a graded cell is
    never the gold answer, so no passing task relies on the old behavior → cannot regress the
    macro class. Fires only on macro-phrased tasks.
- Building on prior RESULTS: kept every load-bearing block from cand_0001–0003. Did NOT re-add
  cand_0004's executed generalization self-test (REJECTED, broke {18137,253-22,347-49,47699,
  50486,53957,56561}) nor cand_0005's key-canonicalization bullet (REJECTED, broke {31420,
  36478,47699,49237,50486,50682,56561}). Both prior rejections ACTIVELY changed agent behavior
  on the general class (extra execution steps / type coercion in matching) and perturbed the
  same near-boundary tasks — my edit deliberately confines its behavioral change to a pattern
  (VBA-source-in-cell) no passing task exhibits.
- Refuted hypotheses (never re-test): global "never use formulas / always literals" — I
  RE-VERIFIED this iteration that 35747/37962/45581/49237/54675 all WRITE formulas (=IF,
  =IFERROR, =COUNTIFS, =LOOKUP) and all pass `[1,1,1]`, so the grader DOES recalc formulas; a
  formula ban regresses those 5. (A diagnostic subagent proposed exactly this rule from 53062;
  I disproved it empirically and dropped it — do NOT resurrect it.) Also refuted: executed
  self-test (cand_0004); key type-canonicalization bullet (cand_0005); re-tightening verify
  item (a) (cand_0001's 399-14 break).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: comprehension `[0,0,0]` (269-44, 146-49, 157-4, 398-14,
  413-15, 577-40, 585-41, 10281, 32468, 39946, 50526, 53449, 55039, 6698, 45944, 55912) — code
  generalizes but implements the WRONG operation; gold-specific (column order/sort, hyphen-vs-0,
  extra sentinel rows, total placement, comma removal, state-machine phase). No gold in traces →
  every prose fix fails VERIFIED/SAFE. Task-specific boundary `[1,0,*]` (250-20 exact-dup dedupe
  vs sum, 42930 tie-break, 30930/32975 group-boundary, 49782, 53305, 58890, 58484, 48983) — no
  shared signature; boundary/run-segment prose already present since cand_0002/0003.
- GRADER/ENVIRONMENT faults handed back (UNWINNABLE by any prompt — the 0.637 champion already
  contains tasks the grader will never pass): 34-5 (output byte-identical to gold on all 3 yet
  0/3), 4225 & 55258 (reproduce the instruction's own stated example yet 0/3), 14207 (harness
  says recalc failed, "not a prompt defect"), 55912 (invalid xlsx), 53062 (formula precedents),
  32023 (unknowable TODAY() reference date).
- Plateau signal: cand_0003 (+0.066) → cand_0004 REJECTED → cand_0005 REJECTED (both -0.077,
  0 fixed). Clean prose surface is exhausted; this iteration extracts the LAST verifiable safe
  additive rule and confines its blast radius. If it doesn't clear the bar, the residual is the
  comprehension + grader-fault ceiling — the honest next step is to hand that back with this
  evidence, NOT to ship speculative comprehension prose (which regressed twice).
- Focus next iteration: if ACCEPTED, confirm 254-34 flipped and no macro task regressed. If
  REJECTED with no regressions, conclude the comprehension/grader ceiling and hand it back with
  the 34-5/4225/55258/14207 evidence. Do NOT re-attempt: formula bans, executed self-tests,
  key-canonicalization, or comprehension-specific prose.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.549 Δ=-0.088 · fixed={50755, 53062} · broke={253-22, 2768, 31420, 347-49, 36478, 45581, 49237, 50486, 53957, 56561}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
<!-- cand_0006: rejected val=0.549 Δ=-0.088 -->

## Iteration cand_0007 — documented CEILING; no speculative edit shipped (capability unchanged vs cand_0003)
- Changes I made: NONE. prompt.md and task_template.md are byte-identical to champion
  cand_0003. After a full re-diagnosis I found no edit that passes REAL+SAFE+VERIFIED and is
  not already refuted; shipping a fourth speculative edit would fail the VERIFIED test and only
  re-perturb the flaky boundary tasks (the exact failure mode of 0004/0005/0006). Expect the
  gate to REJECT (net-zero) and preserve cand_0003 — that is the correct outcome for a ceiling.
- NEW EVIDENCE (this is the value of the iteration): three tasks previously filed as
  "comprehension/flaky" are actually **grader/type-strictness faults where the agent's output
  is provably CORRECT**:
